records.explanation: The link for a network facing adapter interface is down. Cisco UCS Manager raises this fault when any of the following scenarios occur: • Cisco UCS Manager cannot establish and/or validate the adapter's connectivity to any of the fabric interconnects. • The endpoint reports a link down or vNIC down event on the adapter link. • The endpoint reports an errored link state or errored vNIC state event on the adapter link.
records.cause: link-down
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Verify that the adapter is connected, configured properly, and is running the recommended firmware
version.
2. If the server is stuck at discovery, decommission the server and reacknowledge the server slot.
3. If the above actions did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: Fabric Interconnect [id], HA Cluster interconnect link failure
records.explanation: This fault occurs when one of the cluster links (either L1 or L2) of a fabric interconnect is not operationally up. This issue impacts the full HA functionality of the fabric interconnect cluster.
records.cause: link-down
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Verify that both L1 and L2 links are properly connected between the fabric interconnects.
2. If the above action did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

records.cause: link-down
records.recommended_action:

2. If the above action did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: IOM [chassisId]/[id] ([switchId]) current connectivity does not match discovery policy or connectivity is unsupported: [configState]
records.explanation: This fault typically occurs when the current connectivity for an I/O module does not match the configuration in the chassis discovery policy.
records.cause: unsupported-connectivity-configuration
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Verify that the correct number of links are configured in the chassis discovery policy.
2. Check the state of the I/O module links.
3. Note that atleast 2 links are required to be connected between FEX and 61xx Fabric Interconnect
4. Reacknowledge the chassis.
5. If the above action did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: IOM [chassisId]/[id] ([switchId]) is auto upgrading firmware
records.explanation: This fault typically occurs when an I/O module is auto upgrading. Auto-upgrade occurs when the firmware version on the IOM is incompatible with the firmware version on the fabric interconnect.
records.cause: auto-firmware-upgrade
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. If the IOM and fabric interconnects are not running the same firmware version, wait for the auto-upgrade
to complete.
2. When the IOM upgrade is completed, verify that Cisco UCS Manager has cleared this fault.
3. If you see this fault after the IOM overall status changes to operable, create a show tech-support file and
contact Cisco TAC.

messages: Fabric Interconnect [id], management services are unresponsive
records.explanation: This fault occurs when management services on a fabric interconnect are unresponsive. This impacts the full HA functionality of the fabric interconnect cluster.
records.cause: management-services-unresponsive
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Verify that the initial setup configuration is correct on both fabric interconnects.
2. Verify that the L1 and L2 links are properly connected between the fabric interconnects.
3. Reboot the fabric interconnects.
4. If the above actions did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: server pool [name] is empty
records.explanation: This fault typically occurs when the selected server pool does not contain any servers.
records.cause: empty-pool
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Verify the qualifier settings in the server pool policy qualifications. If the policy was modified after the
server was discovered, reacknowledge the server.
2. Manually associate the service profile with a server.
3. If the server pool is not used, ignore the fault.
4. If the above actions did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: Buffer Unit [id] on server [chassisId]/[slotId] temperature: [thermal]Buffer Unit [id] on server [id] temperature: [thermal]Buffer Unit [id] on server [chassisId]/[slotId]/[serverInstanceId] temperature: [thermal]
records.explanation: This fault occurs when the temperature of a memory buffer unit on a blade or rack server exceeds a critical threshold value. Be aware of the following possible contributing factors: • Temperature extremes can cause Cisco UCS equipment to operate at reduced efficiency and cause a variety of problems, including early degradation, failure of chips, and failure of equipment. In addition, extreme temperature fluctuations can cause CPUs to become loose in their sockets. • Cisco UCS equipment should operate in an environment that provides an inlet air temperature not colder than 50F (10C) nor hotter than 95F (35C). • If sensors on a CPU reach 179.6F (82C), the system will take that CPU offline.
records.cause: thermal-problem
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Review the product specifications to determine the temperature operating range of the server.
2. Review the Cisco UCS Site Preparation Guide to ensure the servers have adequate airflow, including front
and back clearance.
3. Verify that the air flows on the Cisco UCS chassis or rack server are not obstructed.
4. Verify that the site cooling system is operating properly.
5. Power off unused blade servers and rack servers.
6. Clean the installation site at regular intervals to avoid buildup of dust and debris, which can cause a system
to overheat.
7. Use the Cisco UCS power capping capability to limit power usage. Power capping can limit the power
consumption of the system, including blade and rack servers, to a threshold that is less than or equal to
the system's maximum rated power. Power-capping can have an impact on heat dissipation and help to
lower the installation site temperature.
8. If the above actions did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: Connection to Management Port [id] in server [id] is missing
records.explanation: This fault occurs when the connectivity between a server and FEX is removed or unconfigured.
records.cause: link-missing
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take the following actions:
1. Check the connectivity between the server and FEX.
2. If the connectivity was changed by mistake, restore it to its previous configuration.
3. If the connectivity change was intentional, reacknowledge the server.
4. If the above actions did not resolve the issue, create a show tech-support file and contact Cisco TAC.

messages: Member [slotId]/[portId] cannot be added to SAN Port-Channel [portId] on fabric interconnect [id], reason: [membership]
records.explanation: This fault typically occurs when the maximum supported Fibre Channel speed of a port in a Fibre Channel port channel is incompatible with the admin speed configured for the port channel.
records.cause: incompatible-speed
records.recommended_action:
If you see this fault, take one of the following actions:
• Change the admin speed of the port channel to match the maximum supported speed of the member ports
in the port channel.
• Replace the expansion module in the fabric interconnect with one that matches the admin speed configured
for the port channel.

messages: device [chassis1], error connecting to shared-storage management interface
records.explanation: This fault occurs in an unlikely event that the shared storage selected for writing the cluster state is not accessible. This fault is typically a transient fault. You might see this fault when one of the following occurs: (a) the Fabric Interconnect boots, (b) the IO Module is reset, (c) the rack server is reboot, or (d) system is upgraded/downgraded. If this fault is not cleared after the system returns to normal operation following the reboot/reset/upgrade/downgrade, then it may affect the full HA functionality of the Fabric Interconnect cluster.

records.recommended_action:

messages: The Multi-Chassis Management group lead redundancy is lost because of either network issues or firmware version mismatch.
records.explanation: The Redundancy feature of the Multi-Chassis Management (MCM) group lead chassis is unavailable anymore either because of network issues or difference in the firmware version of lead and backup chassis.
records.cause: The Redundancy feature of the Multi-Chassis Management (MCM) group lead chassis is unavailable anymore either because of network issues or difference in the firmware version of lead and backup chassis.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the network cables that connect the management ports between the
chassis. 2) Make sure that the firmware version of the lead and backup chassis are same. If the issue
persists, unassign the backup chassis and reassign. For information about assigning a backup chassis,
see the OpenManage Enterprise-Modular Users Guide available on the support site.

records.recommended_action:
Back up the data from the disk. Start disk initialization and wait for it to complete, and then restore
the data from a backup copy.

messages: The global hot-spare drive arg1 does not cover all the virtual drives (VDs) available on the controller.
records.explanation: The global hot-spare identified in the message either does not meet bus protocol, media type, or does not have sufficient storage space to cover all the virtual drives available on the controller.
records.recommended_action: Assign a drive with matching bus protocol, media type, and sufficient storage space.

messages: Bad block table on arg1 is 80% full.
records.explanation: The bad block table is the table used for remapping bad disk blocks. This table fills as bad disk blocks are remapped. When the table is full, bad disk blocks are no longer remapped, which means that disk errors are no longer corrected. At this point, data loss can occur. The bad block table is now 80 percent full.
records.recommended_action: Replace the disk generating this message.

messages: Bad block table on arg1 is full. Unable to log block arg2.
records.explanation: The bad block table is the table used for remapping bad disk blocks. This table fills as bad disk blocks are remapped. When the table is full, bad disk blocks are no longer remapped, which means that disk errors are no longer corrected. At this point, data loss can occur.
records.recommended_action: Replace the disk generating this message and restore from a backup copy. You may have lost data.

messages: arg1 is offline.
records.explanation: A physical disk in the virtual disk is offline. This may have been user initiated.
records.cause: A physical disk in the virtual disk is offline. This may have been user initiated.
records.recommended_action: Force the physical disk online or assign a hot spare to the virtual disk.

messages: The rebuild failed due to errors on the target arg1.
records.explanation: It is not possible to rebuild data that resides on a defective disk.
records.cause: The rebuild failed due to errors on the target arg1.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the target disk. If a rebuild does not automatically start after replacing the disk, then initiate
the Rebuild task. You may need to assign the new disk as a hot spare to initiate the rebuild.

messages: Bad block table on arg1 is full. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: The number of blocks on the disk that exhibit an error has exceeded the capacity of the drive to remap. Any future writes to bad sectors will be unrecoverable.
records.recommended_action: Replace the disk.

messages: System management interrupt initialization failed.
records.explanation: System BIOS failed to initialize the system management interrupt. This exception occurred early in system power on, thus the system may not display video. (BIOS POST exception code 8C) .
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reapply input power. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: System BIOS has halted.
records.explanation: System BIOS has halted and is unable to continue.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) If new hardware has been added, remove the new hardware and restart
the server, 2) Turn server off and back on using the power button, or 3) Remove and reapply server
input power. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: General failure after video.
records.explanation: System BIOS detected a functional or configuration issue during system POST. Check the system video screen for more information. The system event log may contain additional details. This exception occurred early in system power on, thus the system may not display video. (BIOS POST Exception code FE).
records.recommended_action: Check system video and review event log for additional information.

messages: The power input for power supply arg1 is outside of range.
records.explanation: The operating requirements for the power supply may be found in product documentation or on the power supply itself.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the input source is attached to the power supply. Verify the input power is within the operating
requirements for the power supply.

messages: Power supply arg1 is operating at 110 volts, and could cause a circuit breaker fault.
records.explanation: A power supply that is designed to operate at 220V, but is connected to a 110V power source requires additional current for operation. The additional current may trip circuit-breakers or cause other electrical issues with the input source.
records.recommended_action:
Check input power source and cabling. Use recommended input power. Review the product
documentation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Cannot communicate with power supply arg1.
records.explanation: The power supply may operate, however power supply monitoring will be degraded. System performance may be degraded.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and re-install the power supply. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Power supply arg1 vendor type mismatch detected.
records.explanation: Power supplies should be of the same input type and power rating.
records.recommended_action: Install matched power supplies and review product documentation for proper configuration.

messages: Power supply arg1 status is unknown.
records.explanation: The status of the power supply unit identified in the message is unknown, because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power supply unit is not correctly seated. 2) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 3) The power supply unit has failed. 4) There is an input power failure.
records.cause: The status of the power supply unit identified in the message is unknown, because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power supply unit is not correctly seated. 2) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 3) The power supply unit has failed. 4) There is an input power failure.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following to resolve the issue: 1) reseat the power supply unit. 2) Reconnect the power
cable to the power supply unit. 3) Install a new power supply unit 4) Restore the input power supply.

messages: Unable to retrieve PSU arg1 input voltage information.
records.explanation: Unable to retrieve input voltage information for the PSU specified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the PSU from the chassis, wait for two minutes, and reinsert it. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: arg1, PSUarg2 firmware update is in progress.
records.explanation: Unable to set the Power configuration because the PSU firmware update is in progress.
records.cause: Unable to set the Power configuration because the PSU firmware update is in progress.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation after the PSU firmware update is completed.

messages: PSU arg1 reported input under voltage fault and has been turned off.
records.explanation: The power supply unit (PSU) identified in the message was turned off because the input under voltage fault occurred.
records.cause: The power supply unit (PSU) identified in the message was turned off because the input under voltage fault occurred.
records.recommended_action:
1) Check PSU AC input power source. 2) Remove AC power and reapply power to the PSU to get it
functional again. 3) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The Power Supply Unit arg1 reported input overcurrent fault and has been turned off.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) identified in the message was turned off because the input overcurrent fault occurred.
records.cause: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) identified in the message was turned off because the input overcurrent fault occurred.
records.recommended_action:
1) Verify system load is within the Power Supply Unit (PSU) capacity and no short circuits are present
in the system. 2) Press and hold the power button for 30 seconds. The PSU is powered on. 3) If the
issue persists, contact technical support.

messages: Unable to turn on the server because a PCIe card or Mezzanine card is not installed.
records.explanation: The server did not turn on because a PCIe card or Mezzanine card is not installed.
records.cause: The server did not turn on because a PCIe card or Mezzanine card is not installed.
records.recommended_action: Install a PCI or Mezzanine card in the appropriate slot and retry the operation.

messages: Server arg1 power inventory is not valid. Power inventory reading is Max Power=arg2 AC Watt, Min Power=arg3 AC Watt, Allocated Power=arg4 AC Watt.
records.explanation: Invalid power inventory reported by the iDRAC of the server identified in the message to the CMC.
records.recommended_action:
Turn on the server identified in the message. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Successfully completed the iDRAC firmware update. All current user sessions will be closed.
records.explanation: The message appears in Job Queue page when the iDRAC firmware update job status is completed. Communication to the iDRAC will be lost .
records.recommended_action: The iDRAC will be ready for login once the restart is complete.

messages: This setting will be applied during the next server restart. If the setting is not compatible with the RAID Controller, then LED status indicators on all the associated hard disk drives (HDDs) stop functioning.
records.explanation: This setting will be applied during the next server restart. If the setting is not compatible with the RAID Controller, then LED status indicators on all the associated hard disk drives (HDDs) stop functioning.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: Invalid value for Minimum Fan Speed.
records.explanation: The value for Minimum Fan Speed must be within the range identified in the Recommended Response Action.
records.recommended_action: Enter a value between <min>-<max>.

messages: The Secure Erase command will be executed on the selected PCIe SSD disk drives(s) only after the reboot of the system or loss of power to the disk drives(s).
records.explanation: A Secure Erase operation on a PCIe SSD overwrites all blocks in an encrypted way and all the data on the PCIe SSD device will be permanently lost. The changes will happen after reboot of the system or loss of power to the drive.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: The BIOS watchdog timer must be disabled if the Automatic System Recovery option is enabled.
records.explanation: The BIOS watchdog must be disabled if Automatic System Recovery option is enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the BIOS watchdog timer is disabled before enabling the Automatic System Recovery
option.

messages: Unable to access the USB NIC IP address by using PING process.
records.explanation: The USB NIC IP address cannot be accessed by using the PING process.
records.recommended_action: Enter another appropriate IP address, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to change the auto-negotiation state for the current NIC selection mode.
records.explanation: Unable to change the auto-negotiation state for the current NIC selection mode, because the iDRAC NIC is in dedicated mode.
records.cause: Unable to change the auto-negotiation state for the current NIC selection mode, because the iDRAC NIC is in dedicated mode.
records.recommended_action:
Change the iDRAC NIC mode to shared mode using "racadm set idrac.nic.selection <value>", and retry
the operation.

messages: Unable to add the FQDD to the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the list is full.
records.explanation: The FQDD cannot be added to the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the list is full.
records.cause: The FQDD cannot be added to the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the list is full.
records.recommended_action: Delete any unused or unwanted FQDDs from the list and retry the operation.

messages: The entered option is not supported by the interface.
records.explanation: The requested file can be exported from the firmware racadm only to a remote file share.
records.recommended_action:
Create a remote file share to export the file or use remote or local racadm to export to the file system
that is accessible by the racadm executable.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because the Secure Boot policy is of unknown type.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is of unknown type.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is of unknown type.
records.recommended_action:
Set the Secure Boot policy to Standard or Custom mode. For example to set the policy to Custom
mode use command "racadm set bios.syssecurity.securebootpolicy Custom". For more information,
see the RACADM CLI Reference Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to update the arg1 firmware because of connection issues. Code arg2.
records.explanation: The firmware version of the component cannot be updated because of connection issues.
records.cause: The firmware version of the component cannot be updated because of connection issues.
records.recommended_action:
The firmware version of component identified in the message cannot be updated because of
connection issues. Refer to the documentation on the support site for interpretation of the error
code.

messages: Invalid object value specified.
records.explanation: The dedicated NIC or shared NIC scan time value is not between 5 and 255 seconds.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure to set the scan time value between 5 and 255 seconds, and retry the operation. For more
information, see RACADM help.

messages: arg1 value has dropped below the lower warning limit.
records.explanation: To update the user that the sensor value is less than the lower warning threshold.
records.recommended_action: Inspect the sensor described in the message.

messages: arg1 value has exceeded the upper warning limit.
records.explanation: To update the user that the sensor value is greater than the upper warning threshold.
records.recommended_action: Inspect the sensor described in the message.

messages: Unable to update the firmware version because the license version of the currently installed firmware does not allow the update process.
records.explanation: The firmware version cannot be updated because the license version of the currently installed firmware does not allow the update process.
records.cause: The firmware version cannot be updated because the license version of the currently installed firmware does not allow the update process.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the recommended license is installed, and then retry updating the firmware. For
information about compatible license versions, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support
site.

messages: The reinstallfw command has failed due to unavailability of the firmware image.
records.explanation: iDRAC internal firmware volume does not have any firmware image. So reinstallfw command has failed.
records.cause: The reinstallfw command has failed due to unavailability of the firmware image.
records.recommended_action: Please update the firmware using DUP.

messages: Removable Flash Media is not ready.
records.explanation: The media is being prepared or is under maintenance. If the problem persists, reinstall the card.
records.recommended_action: If unintended, reinstall the flash media.

messages: Processor detected a problem while performing an Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT) operation.
records.explanation: TXT CPU microcode boot cannot be completed because system configuration may have changed.
records.cause: TXT CPU microcode boot cannot be completed because system configuration may have changed.
records.recommended_action:
Check system hardware inventory for TPM presence, clear and reconfigure TPM and TXT in BIOS
setup menu.

messages: BIOS Authenticated Code Module detected an Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT) problem during POST.
records.explanation: TXT POST cannot be completed because system configuration may have changed.
records.cause: TXT POST cannot be completed because system configuration may have changed.
records.recommended_action:
Check system hardware inventory for TPM presence, clear and reconfigure TPM and TXT in BIOS
setup menu.

messages: Unable to complete the Key Purge operation at the KMS because either iDRAC could not communicate to the KMS or failed to locate the keys. arg1 keys are successfully purged. arg2 could not be purged.
records.explanation: A Key Purge operations is invoked after a Rekey operation or when the SEKM feature is disabled after enabling the Key Purge feature. When performing the Rekey operation, iDRAC will purge all unused keys except the current and previous keys. The current key is the newly generated key and the previous key is the key that was in use before the Rekey operation. After disabling the SEKM feature, all keys generated by this iDRAC are purged.
records.cause: Unable to complete the Key Purge operation at the KMS because either iDRAC could not communicate to the KMS or failed to locate the keys. arg1 keys are successfully purged. arg2 could not be purged.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. During the next Rekey operation, iDRAC will attempt to purge the
remaining keys. However, if the purge operations consecutively fails then manually delete these
unused keys.

messages: iDRAC is unable to do a PSID based revert on the device arg1. Error response arg2.
records.explanation: iDRAC was unable to erase a secured drive using the provided PSID and data is accessible on the drive.
records.recommended_action:
1) Ensure that the device supports the security protocol support viaSMBus (TCG Opal or TCG
Enterprise).2) Ensure that the Security Send/Receivecommands are supported via SMBus.3) Ensure
that the device has the latestfirmware.

messages: iDRAC has used the cached key because iDRAC could not connect to the Key Management Server.
records.explanation: Indicates that iDRAC has used the locally cached key to unlock secured devices. This is because iDRAC was unable to start communication with the external Key Management Server for the specified KMSConnectionTimeout value.
records.cause: Indicates that iDRAC has used the locally cached key to unlock secured devices. This is because iDRAC was unable to start communication with the external Key Management Server for the specified KMSConnectionTimeout value.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following steps:1) Make sure that the network connection is available between Key
Management Server and iDRAC.2) Make sure that iDRAC has access to the required key ID on the
Key Management Server.

messages: The performance of CPUarg1 is automatically readjusted by Chassis Controller because of unacceptable change in the thermal and power conditions.
records.explanation: The performance of the CPU identified in the message is automatically readjusted by the Chassis Manager(CM) because of an unacceptable change in the thermal and power conditions. This issue is reported when the power cableis disconnected from the PSU, and it also depends on the residual power to log in to the server.
records.cause: The performance of the CPU identified in the message is automatically readjusted by the Chassis Manager(CM) because of an unacceptable change in the thermal and power conditions. This issue is reported when the power cableis disconnected from the PSU, and it also depends on the residual power to log in to the server.
records.recommended_action:
Check the firmware version of Chassis Manager(CM) and make sure that the Power Supply Unit
(PSU) is functional.

messages: Unable to synchronize arg1 Settings between arg2. Power loss detection redundancy is degraded.
records.explanation: NVDIMM Settings could not be synchronized across Management Modules.
records.recommended_action:
Reboot from OME - Modular GUI, physically reseat or initiate a firmware update on the standby
Management Module.

messages: A firmware mismatch detected in arg1.
records.explanation: An action or failure has taken place that breaks redundancy in the Management Module. The message identifies the exact cause.
records.recommended_action: Initiate a firmware update from Management Module UI for the component identified in the message.

messages: A firmware version mismatch is detected between two hot-swappable expanders within the Storage enclosure.
records.explanation: A firmware version mismatch is detected between two hot-swappable expanders within the Storage enclosure.
records.recommended_action:
Update the expander firmware. For information about managing SAS IOM devices, refer to
OpenManage Enterprise Modular Version Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: No batteries are displayed.
records.explanation: No battery data to display. The system is powered off, batteries are not present on the system, batteries are not connected to the RAID controller, or the batteries are depleted.
records.recommended_action:
Check if the server has power, batteries are available, and batteries are connected to the RAID
controller.

messages: Temperature probes are not connected to enclosures or data about temperature is unavailable.
records.explanation: No temperature data to display. The system is powered off, no enclosure temperature probes are present in the system, or the temperature probes are not connected to the enclosures.
records.recommended_action:
Check if the server has power, enclosure temperature probe is available, and temperature probe is
connected to the enclosure.

messages: Unable to monitor or manage SAS components because the initialization sequence of the devices did not complete.
records.explanation: The initialization sequence of SAS components did not complete during system startup.
records.cause: Unable to monitor or manage SAS components because the initialization sequence of the devices did not complete.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Make sure that the supported versions of the SAS drivers and firmware are
installed. 2) Reboot the system. If problem persists, reinstall Server Administrator and Storage
Services on the managed node to make sure all the required components are installed.

messages: No RAID levels are supported.
records.explanation: The controller does not have the minimum number of initialized disks to create a virtual disk.
records.recommended_action: Connect required number of initialized physical disks to the RAID controller and retry the operation.

messages: One or more physical disks specified are full and cannot be used to create additional virtual disks.
records.explanation: One or more physical disks specified are full and cannot be used to create additional virtual disks.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure all physical disks specified to create a virtual disk have the required amount of free space
and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to change the controller mode because there are already pending operations.
records.explanation: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it requires a server reboot for changes to apply.
records.cause: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it requires a server reboot for changes to apply.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Create a job to complete the pending operations, allow the job to complete,
and then retry the operation. 2) Cancel any pending operations on the RAID controller, and then retry
the operation.

messages: Unable to change controller mode while Virtual Disks and/or Hotspares are present on the controller.
records.explanation: Controller mode cannot be changed as the controller has virtual disk or hotspare associated with it.
records.recommended_action: Delete the Virtual Disks and/or Hotspares and retry the operation.

messages: Controller is in HBA mode, RaidAction CreateAuto value is not supported.
records.explanation: The Controller is in HBA mode, RaidAction CreateAuto value is not supported.
records.recommended_action:
In order to perform a RAID configuration operation, change the controller mode to RAID and retry
the operation. For switching to RAID mode using the F2 System Setup utility, go to Device Settings
> "RAID Controller "> Controller Management > Advanced Controller Management > Switch to RAID
mode.

messages: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the storage controller does not support reconfiguration of a Virtual Disk that is part of a disk group that has multiple Virtual Disks.
records.explanation: This occurs when a disk group is sliced to create multiple Virtual Disks. Reconfiguration of such sliced Virtual Disks is not supported.
records.cause: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the storage controller does not support reconfiguration of a Virtual Disk that is part of a disk group that has multiple Virtual Disks.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the physical disk group has a single Virtual Disk and retry the reconfiguration
operation.

messages: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the number of physical disks specified in the disk group is not as per the permitted range.
records.explanation: A disk drive group has a limit on the minimum and maximum number of disk drives it can have on the basis of its Virtual Disk RAID level. When a reconfiguration operation is specified with additional physical disks the total number of physical disks should be in the disk groups permissible range.
records.cause: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the number of physical disks specified in the disk group is not as per the permitted range.
records.recommended_action:
Enter the correct number of physical disks for the reconfiguration operation and retry the operation.
The number of physical disks in a disk group must be within the disk groups permissible range. For
information about the minimum and maximum possible physical disks in a disk group, see the Lifecycle
Controller Users Guide available at the support site.

messages: Unable to change the controller unmap state because there are already pending operations.
records.explanation: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it requires a server reboot for changes to apply.
records.cause: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it requires a server reboot for changes to apply.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Create a job to complete the pending operations, allow the job to complete,
and then retry the operation. 2) Cancel any pending operations on the RAID controller, and then retry
the operation.

messages: Unable to update the firmware on the arg1 controller because one or more of the following reasons: a) Mismatch in the image file key. b) Unsuccessful authentication. c) Incorrect checksum value.
records.explanation: The firmware on the controller identified in the message cannot be updated because one or more of the following reasons: a) Mismatch in the image file key. b) Unsuccessful authentication. c) Incorrect checksum value.
records.cause: The firmware on the controller identified in the message cannot be updated because one or more of the following reasons: a) Mismatch in the image file key. b) Unsuccessful authentication. c) Incorrect checksum value.
records.recommended_action: Download the latest controller firmware version from the support site, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to locate firmware image file in specified path.
records.explanation: There is no firmware image present at the specified path.
records.recommended_action: Check if the firmware image is present at the specified path.

messages: Unable to update the firmware version because one or more features that do not support the Firmware Update feature are currently enabled.
records.explanation: The firmware version cannot be updated because one or more features that do not support the Firmware Update feature are currently enabled.
records.cause: The firmware version cannot be updated because one or more features that do not support the Firmware Update feature are currently enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the features that do not support the Rollback feature are disabled, and then retry the
operation. For example, if PERC SEKM is enabled then updating to a firmware version that does not
support SEKM is not allowed. Therefore, disable SEKM on iDRAC or remove the SEKM-enabled PERC
controller, and then try the rollback operation.

messages: Unable to install update packages because of insufficient space in the iDRAC.
records.explanation: The update packages cannot be installed because of insufficient space in the iDRAC even after deleting firmware installation files stored in the Rollback feature.
records.cause: The update packages cannot be installed because of insufficient space in the iDRAC even after deleting firmware installation files stored in the Rollback feature.
records.recommended_action:
Delete Lifecycle Controller related data by using the Repurpose or Retire System features, and then
retry the operation.

messages: Unable to recover the arg1 firmware data from the USB drive. See the message:SUP0702.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message cannot be recovered from the USB drive.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure the following and retry the action. Current Options available are:1) USB must be connected
to rear top USB Port.2) Ensure recommended folder structure is followed.3) USB must have one
partition and it should be ext4 or FAT.4) Ensure compatible recovery firmware is present in USB.

messages: A firmware or software incompatibility is detected between arg1arg2 and arg3arg4.
records.explanation: The system has detected a firmware or software incompatibility between the components identified in the message. A mismatch between component versions may cause the system to not function appropriately.
records.recommended_action:
Update the firmware or software of the components identified in the message. For information about
the identified components, see the product documentation available at the service provider support
site.

messages: BIOS image verification failed.
records.explanation: BIOS image verification failed. The BIOS image file recovery operation is initiated.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. For specific issue-related information, see the Lifecycle Log data, and
then initiate necessary corrective action.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of the chassis Power Supply Unit (PSU) because one or more sleds installed on the chassis are currently powered on.
records.explanation: The firmware of the chassis Power Supply Unit (PSU) cannot be updated because one or more sleds installed on the chassis are currently powered on.
records.cause: The firmware of the chassis Power Supply Unit (PSU) cannot be updated because one or more sleds installed on the chassis are currently powered on.
records.recommended_action:
Power off all the sleds in the chassis and then retry the operation. For information about powering off
sleds, see the hardware documentation of the chassis available on the support site.

messages: iDRAC cannot authenticate the LOM firmware because of an internal issue.
records.explanation: iDRAC cannot authenticate the LOM firmware because of an internal issue.
records.recommended_action:
Update the LOM firmware to the latest available version, and then perform a cold-reboot operation on
the server. For information about updating the LOM firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on
the Dell support site. If the issue persists, restart iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to complete the CPLD auto-recovery operation because of an internal error.
records.explanation: One or more CPLDs could not be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue. BMC FW was unable to automatically recover them because of an internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CPLD version using the latest Update Package. The host server will be unavailable until
the update operation is complete.

messages: Unable to authenticate the arg1 firmware because of an internal issue.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message cannot be authenticated because of an internal issue.
records.recommended_action:
1) If the issue is related to LOM or BOSS card associated with iDRAC then perform the Cold Reboot
operation on the server. 2) If the issue is related to Floating OCP Paddle (FLOP) card associated with
iDRAC then perform a Virtual AC Cycle or AC Cycle operation on the server.

messages: The firmware update operation of the iDRAC on the server in slot arg1 was stopped. The selected Image file is not compatible with the server hardware.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of iDRAC identified in the message was stopped. The selected Image file is not compatible with the server hardware.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the Image file is compatible with the server hardware, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the PSU firmware, because the Image file is not accessible. ErrorCode=0xarg1.
records.explanation: The PSU firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred.
records.cause: The PSU firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the PSU firmware image file is available at the location specified in the operation, and
then retry the operation.

messages: Invalid firmware: The uploaded firmware image validation was unsuccessful.

The Secure Boot policy consists of authorized and unauthorized X.509 certificates; signed boot images must chain to an authorized certificate. The policy may also authorize hash values of individual boot images. Users can configure the Secure Boot feature and the Secure Boot policy in System Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page.
records.cause: Unable to boot arg1 because of the Secure Boot policy.
records.recommended_action:

Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page. The boot option must be authorized by a public key
or hash value in the Authorized Signature Database. 2) If the boot option is not authorized but it can
be trusted, enter System Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page, set Secure Boot Policy to
Custom, and add a entry for the boot option in the Authorized Signature Database (System Setup >
System BIOS > Security Settings > Custom Policy Settings > Authorized Signature Database > Import
Database Entry).

records.cause: A drive predictive failure condition was detected.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the drives when conditions permit. For more information, see the server maintenance and service
guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: 1733-Slot # Drive Array – Storage Enclosure Firmware Upgrade Problem Detected
messages: 1733-Slot # Drive Array – Storage Enclosure Firmware Upgrade Problem Detected. Port # Box # (Followed by one of the following:) • Enclosure firmware upgrade needed - run Flash Components. • Unable to read firmware version of one or more components.
records.cause:
•  An incorrect enclosure firmware version is installed.
•  An enclosure firmware upgrade is needed.
•  An enclosure component has failed.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Upgrade the enclosure firmware and the controller firmware.
For more information, see "Firmware updates" in the HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting Guide,
Volume I on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.
2.  If the issue persists, replace the affected enclosure components.

event_names: 1734-Slot # Drive Array – Disk Drive(s) Responding to Incorrect SCSI ID
messages: 1734-Slot # Drive Array – Disk Drive(s) Responding to Incorrect SCSI ID. Back up data, Replace faulty drive, Reconfigure array, and Restore.
records.cause: The drive has failed.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Back up the data on the hard drive.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.
2.  Replace the drive.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.
3.  Reconfigure the array.
For more information, see the HPE Smart Storage Administrator User Guide on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.
4.  Restore data to the new hard drive.

messages: 1736-HP Trusted Platform Module Error.
records.cause: A TPM is installed, but the System ROM is unable to communicate with the TPM.
records.recommended_action:
Request a new system board and TPM board from an authorized service provider. For more information,
see "HPE Trusted Platform Module issues" in the HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting Guide, Volume I on
the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: 1748-Slot # Drive Array – Unsupported Cache Module Battery Attached
messages: 1748-Slot # Drive Array – Unsupported Cache Module Battery Attached. Please install battery pack(s) with the correct part number.
records.cause: The current HPE Smart Storage Battery is not supported on this cache module.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Use the part number to verify that the component is supported.
For a list of supported options, see the product QuickSpecs on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website.
2.  Install a supported HPE Smart Storage Battery.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: 1753-Slot X Drive Array – Array Controller Maximum Operating Temperature Exceeded
messages: 1753-Slot X Drive Array – Array Controller Maximum Operating Temperature Exceeded During Previous Power Up.
records.cause: The controller is overheating.
records.recommended_action:
Be sure adequate system cooling and sufficient airflow across the controller are available. For more
information on optimal space and airflow requirements, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.

messages: 1785-Slot XX Not Configured. SAS cable configuration is invalid. Action: See User’s Guide for supported cabling guidelines.
records.cause: Connections between the drives or controllers are missing or incorrect.
records.recommended_action:
Verify connections between the drives, backplanes, and controller. For more information, see the server
user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 1810-Slot X Encryption Failure-Master Key is incorrect or not retrieved from Remote Key Manager. Encrypted logical drives may be offline. System may not boot.
records.cause:
iLO is unable to communicate with the Remote Key License Server due to a network or configuration issue.
Smart Array Drive Encryption cannot get the authentication keys to decrypt the drives.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check the network connection between the iLO management port and the remote key manager.
2.  Verify that the remote key manager configuration settings in iLO are properly configured.
3.  If the issue persists, update the iLO, Smart Array, and System ROM to the latest versions.
For more information, see the following topic in the troubleshooting guide for your product on the
Hewlett Packard Enterprise website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10—"Keeping the system current" (https://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-
troubleshooting)
•  HPE Synergy—"Updating the firmware" (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)

messages: 1821–Slot X Encryption Failure – FW version for this controller does not support HP Secure Encryption. Encrypted logical drives are offline. System may not boot. Action: Upgrade the FW on this controller.
records.cause: The firmware installed does not support HPE Secure Encryption.
records.recommended_action:
Upgrade the firmware on this controller. For more information, see "Firmware updates" in the HPE
ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting Guide, Volume I on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: 1827-Slot X Drive Array – Please install cache module battery pack
messages: 1827-Slot X Drive Array – Please install cache module battery pack. Caching will be enabled once Battery Pack is installed and charged.
records.cause: The HPE Smart Storage Battery is not installed or not connected correctly.
records.recommended_action:
Install and charge the HPE Smart Storage Battery.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: 1829-Slot # Drive Array – Please replace cache module battery pack
messages: 1829-Slot # Drive Array – Please replace cache module battery pack. Caching will be enabled once the Battery Pack has been replaced and charged.
records.cause: The HPE Smart Storage Battery is not functioning or is not charged.
records.recommended_action:
Replace and charge the HPE Smart Storage Battery.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website.

event_names: 222-DIMM Configuration Error – The DIMM configuration is incorrect
messages: 222-DIMM Configuration Error – The DIMM configuration is incorrect and prevents the system from initializing memory. System video output may have additional information regarding failure. The system is halted.
records.cause:
Memory is not installed correctly.
CAUTION:
Failure to properly handle DIMMs can damage the DIMM components and
the system board connector. For more information, see the DIMM handling
guidelines in the troubleshooting guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (https://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-
troubleshooting)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)
records.recommended_action:
Install DIMMs in a supported configuration.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://
www.hpe.com/info/enterprise-docs).

event_names: 235-Unsupported DIMM Configuration Detected – Mixed DIMM configurations are not supported on this system
messages: 235-Unsupported DIMM Configuration Detected – Mixed DIMM configurations are not supported on this system. (Major Code: X, Minor Code: Y).
records.cause:
DIMMs are installed in an unsupported configuration.
CAUTION:
Failure to properly handle DIMMs can damage the DIMM components and
the system board connector. For more information, see the DIMM handling
guidelines in the troubleshooting guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (https://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-
troubleshooting)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)
records.recommended_action:
Install DIMMs in a supported configuration.
For more information, see the memory population rules on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website
(https://www.hpe.com/docs/memory-population-rules).
For additional information, see the server user guide for your product:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (https://www.hpe.com/info/proliantgen10-docs)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs)

messages: 238-Unsupported DIMM Configuration Detected - Mixing 3DS LRDIMMs with non-3DS LRDIMMs is not supported. (Major Code: X, Minor Code: Y).
records.cause:
DIMMS are installed in an unsupported configuration.

Failure to properly handle DIMMs can damage the DIMM components and
the system board connector. For more information, see the DIMM handling
guidelines in the troubleshooting guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website:

troubleshooting)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)
records.recommended_action:
Install DIMMs in a supported configuration.

•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (https://www.hpe.com/info/proliantgen10-docs)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs)

messages: 259-Unsupported Processor Configuration Detected. All installed processors do not have the same model number.
records.cause:
Processors with different model numbers are installed.
CAUTION:
Before removing or replacing any processors, be sure to follow the guidelines
in "Processor troubleshooting guidelines" in the troubleshooting guide for your
product. Failure to follow the recommended guidelines can cause damage to the
system board, requiring replacement of the system board.
records.recommended_action:
Replace any processors that are not of the same model number.
For more information, see the server user guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (https://www.hpe.com/info/proliantgen10-docs)
•  HPE Synergy (https://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs)

messages: 268-UEFI Non-Volatile Variable Store Corruption Detected. If enabled, Secure Boot security settings may be lost.
records.cause:
A server was interrupted while writing to NVRAM by one of the following:
•  A sudden removal of power
•  Pressing the power button
•  Pressing the iLO virtual power button
records.recommended_action:
1.  Reset any configuration settings that differ from the default settings.
2.  If the issue persists, open a support case using the Hewlett Packard Enterprise Support Center
website (https://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc).

messages: 308-Required Fan NOT Installed – Fan X Missing.
records.cause: A required fan is missing.
records.recommended_action:
Install the indicated fan.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 309-Insufficient Fan Solution. The system does not have the minimum required number of operating fans. Some instances of this message will be followed by "System Halted" when the system is halted during POST
records.cause: The number of fans installed in the server does not meet minimum requirements.
records.recommended_action:
Install the minimum required fans to prevent possible damage to system components.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 317-Chassis Firmware Error – Unable to communicate with the Chassis Firmware. Action: Reset iLO FW. If issue persists reset Chassis FW (remove AC to chassis). If issue persists attempt to update the Chassis FW.
records.cause: A communication issue exists within iLO or the chassis firmware.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Reset the iLO firmware.
For more information, see the iLO user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.
2.  If the issue persists, remove power from the chassis.
3.  If the issue persists, update the chassis firmware.
For more information, see "Keeping the system current" in the HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting
Guide, Volume I on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 325-HP Dual microSD Device Error – microSD cards have conflicting metadata. Configuration required.
records.cause: A microSD card is not configured correctly.
records.recommended_action:
Enter System Utilities and configure the primary microSD card using the System Configuration options.
For more information, see "UEFI System Utilities" in the HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting Guide,
Volume I on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 331-Memory Board Configuration Error – The system contains multiple types of memory boards. Mixing types is NOT supported. – System Halted
records.cause: More than one type of memory board is installed.
records.recommended_action:
Install only one type of memory board.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 332-Memory Board Configuration Error – One or more installed memory boards is of a type NOT supported by the installed processor. – System Halted
records.cause: An unsupported memory board is installed.
records.recommended_action:
Remove any memory boards not supported by the installed processor.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 341-NVDIMM Error – Restore Error - Processor X, DIMM Y. Persistent data restore failed and data is not available.
records.cause:
•  The restore operation, copying data from NVDIMM-N flash memory to NVDIMM-N DRAM, did not
complete successfully.
•  The NVDIMM has failed.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the NVDIMM.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website.

messages: 359-NVDIMM Population Error – Processor 1 must have at least one RDIMM installed when NVDIMMs are present in the system. Action: Install an RDIMM on Processor 1.
records.cause: At least one standard DIMM is not installed on Processor 1, as required in the population guidelines.
records.recommended_action:
Install a regular DIMM on Processor 1.
For more information, see the server user guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.
When HPE 8 GB NVDIMMs are installed in a server, all regular DIMMs in the server must be RDIMMs. For
more information, see the HPE 8GB NVDIMM User Guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

messages: 363-Memory Initialization Error – Processor X, DIMM Y failed initialization. Action: Reseat the processor and DIMM. Call Service if issue persists. – System Halted!
records.cause: The processor or DIMM is installed incorrectly.
records.recommended_action:
CAUTION:
Before removing or replacing any processors, be sure to follow the
processor troubleshooting guidelines in "Performing Processor Procedures
in the Troubleshooting Process" in the HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting
Guide, Volume I: Troubleshooting. Failure to follow the recommended
guidelines can cause damage to the system board, requiring replacement
of the system board.
1.  Reseat the processor.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.
2.  Reseat the DIMM.
3.  If the issue persists, contact Hewlett Packard Enterprise support.
For more information, see "Accessing Hewlett Packard Enterprise support."

messages: 387-NVDIMM Error – Processor X, DIMM Y. NVDIMM Metadata is corrupted. NVDIMM is disabled.
records.cause:
The data on the NVDIMM metadata that defines how the NVDIMM is used in the server is corrupt in a
server with NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Sanitize the NVDIMM.
For more information, see the HPE 16GB NVDIMM User Guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website
(https://www.hpe.com/info/NVDIMM-docs).

event_names: Cache module: The cache is disabled because the batteries are low on the redundant controller
messages: Cache module: The cache is disabled because the batteries are low on the redundant controller.
records.cause: The batteries are not charged.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the batteries if the batteries do not recharge within 36 powered-on hours.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website.

event_names: Cache module: The cache is disabled because the restore operation from flash memory failed
messages: Cache module: The cache is disabled because the restore operation from flash memory failed.
records.cause: The restore operation did not complete.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Reseat the controller cache module.
2.  If the issue persists, contact Hewlett Packard Enterprise support. For more information, see
"Accessing Hewlett Packard Enterprise support."

event_names: Logical drive state: This logical drive has a high physical drive count
messages: Logical drive state: This logical drive has a high physical drive count as well as a high stripe size value such that a controller lock up could occur. It is recommended that the stripe size be migrated to a lower value.
records.cause:
A logical drive has a high physical drive count and a high stripe size value that can lead to a controller
lockup.
records.recommended_action:
Migrate the stripe size to a lower value using the HPE SSA.
For more information, see the HPE Smart Storage Administrator User Guide on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.

event_names: Physical Drive State: This drive is not supported for configuration by this version of controller firmware
messages: Physical Drive State: This drive is not supported for configuration by this version of controller firmware.
records.cause: The controller firmware version does not support the drive.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical drive with a drive supported by the controller. To locate a supported option, review
the product QuickSpecs on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: Physical Drive State: This drive is unrecognizable
messages: Physical Drive State: This drive is unrecognizable. It is not supported for configuration and should be disconnected from this controller.
records.cause: The drive is not supported.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical drive with a drive supported by the controller. To locate a supported option, review
the product QuickSpecs on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website.

event_names: Storage Enclosure: One or more fans have failed
messages: Storage Enclosure: One or more fans have failed.
records.cause: One or more fans have failed.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the fan.
For more information, see the maintenance and service guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard
Enterprise website.

messages: 8012 - FC Fabric state FAILED
records.explanation: The VC fabric lost all uplink connectivity because of lack of configured ports or all configured ports are in a bad state.
records.cause:
•  The VC fabric has no configured ports. The user removed all the uplink ports from the fabric.
•  ALL VC fabric ports are in one of the following states:
◦ FAILED (hardware error), UNAVAILABLE (not logged in), DISABLED, UNKNOWN (FC module NO-
COMM).
◦ There is no uplink that is in DEGRADED or OK state.
records.recommended_action: Configure the uplink ports.

event_names: Connectivity has been lost for the NIC in slot %1, port %2.
messages: Connectivity has been lost for the NIC in slot %1, port %2.
records.explanation: This trap is sent any time the status of a logical adapter changes to the Failed condition. This occurs when the adapter in a single adapter configuration fails, or when the last adapter in a redundant configuration fails. This can be caused by loss of link due to a cable being removed from the adapter or the Hub or Switch. Internal adapter, Hub, or Switch failures can also cause this condition.
records.cause: This trap is sent any time the status of a logical adapter changes to the Failed condition. This occurs when the adapter in a single adapter configuration fails, or when the last adapter in a redundant configuration fails. This can be caused by loss of link due to a cable being removed from the adapter or the Hub or Switch. Internal adapter, Hub, or Switch failures can also cause this condition.
records.recommended_action:
Check the cables to the adapter and the Hub or Switch. If no cable problems are found, the
adapter, Hub, or Switch may need replacement.

event_names: Storage System Fault Tolerant Power Supply Degraded.
messages: The fault tolerant power supply in the %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in slot %4 has a degraded status. Restore power or replace any failed power supply.
records.explanation: A storage system power supply status has been set to degraded.
records.recommended_action: Restore power or replace any failed storage system power supply.

messages: The Drive Array Controller in slot %4 has become the active controller.
records.explanation: Controller Active. This trap indicates that the agent has detected that a backup array controller in a duplexed pair has switched over to the active role. The variable cpqDaCntlrSlot indicates the active controller slot, and cpqDaCntlrPartnerSlot indicates the backup.
records.recommended_action:
Check the partner controller for problems. If this was the result of a user initiated switch-over,
no action is required.

event_names: Storage System Fault Tolerant Power Supply Status Change.
messages: The fault tolerant power supply in the %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in %4 has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Storage System Fault Tolerant Power Supply Status Change. The agent has detected a change in the power supply status of a storage system. The variable cpqSsBoxFltTolPwrSupplyStatus indicates the current power supply status.
records.recommended_action: If the power supply status is degraded, restore power or replace the failed power supply.

event_names: Storage System Fault Tolerant Power Supply Status Change.
messages: The fault tolerant power supply in the %6 %7 storage system connected to %5 of the controller in%4 has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Storage System Fault Tolerant Power Supply Status Change. The agent has detected a change in the power supply status of a storage system. The variable cpqSsBoxFltTolPwrSupplyStatus indicates the current power supply status.
records.recommended_action: If the power supply status is degraded, restore power or replace the failed power supply.

messages: This trap indicates that an enclosure fan has failed but other fans in the redundant fan group are still operating. This may result in overheating of the enclosure.
records.explanation: The enclosure fan status has been set to degraded. This trap indicates that an enclosure fan has failed but that other fans in the redundant fan group are still operating. This may result in the enclosure overheating.
records.recommended_action: Replace the fan as soon as possible.

event_names: %1 Storage system overheating (%2Slot %3, Temperature Sensor %4, Location %5, Temperature %6)
messages: %1 Storage system overheating (%2Slot %3, Temperature Sensor %4, Location %5, Temperature %6)
records.cause:
•  The processor heatsink is not installed as indicated in the server documentation.
•  A supported fan is not installed in the server.
•  An air baffle or blank is missing or not installed properly and causing a disruption of the airflow.
records.recommended_action:
Check Fans, processor heat sink, and air baffles installation.
1.  Verify that all air baffles and required blanks, such as drive blanks, processor heat sink blanks, power
supply blanks, and so on, are installed.
2.  Verify that the correct processor heat sink is installed.
3.  Verify that the correct fan is installed, if the system supports both standard fans and performance
fans.
For additional information, see the system documentation.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: The temperature of the PCIe disk %1 has crossed the upper critical threshold.
records.cause: The temperature of the disk has crossed the upper critical threshold.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check the system for hardware failures.
2.  If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
a.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed.
For specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance
and service guide.
b.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: Liquid Cooling Module Degraded (%1, Location %2)
records.cause:
1.  One or more Liquid cooling modules are not seated properly.
2.  One or more required Liquid cooling modules are not installed.
3.  One or more Liquid cooling modules are not functioning.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure that the liquid cooling module configuration meets the functional requirements of the server.
For more information, see the server maintenance and service guide for your product on the Hewlett
Packard Enterprise website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (http://www.hpe.com/info/proliantgen10-docs)
•  HPE Synergy (http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs)

event_names: Processor %1 encountered fault or an unrecoverable error while booting (before SCP boot) - Restart Initiated
messages: Processor %1 encountered fault or an unrecoverable error while booting (before SCP boot) - Restart Initiated
records.cause: Processor encountered a fault or unrecoverable error while booting (before SCP boot)
records.recommended_action:
BMC automatically initiates a system cold boot. If it does not recover, then reposition the processor and
update to the latest firmware. If the issue persists contact the support
1.  Review any recent BIOS Firmware update or Customer Errata available related to this event.
2.  Remove and re-insert the Processor installed on the socket specified in the IML description

event_names: An uncorrectable processor error detected (Processor: %1, Error Type: %2, Error count: %3%4)
messages: An uncorrectable processor error detected (Processor: %1, Error Type: %2, Error count: %3%4)
records.cause: An uncorrectable processor error detected.
records.recommended_action: System performs an auto-reset to recover from the error. Contact support team if the issue persists.

event_names: PCI Express Uncorrectable Error Detected (Processor: %1, Segment: %2, AER Uncorrectable Error Status: %3, Overflow: %4)
messages: PCI Express Uncorrectable Error Detected (Processor: %1, Segment: %2, AER Uncorrectable Error Status: %3, Overflow: %4)
records.cause: PCIe uncorrectable error detected
records.recommended_action: Update the firmware of the device. If the issue persists please contact support team

event_names: An uncorrectable PCI express error detected on Port type: %1 (Segment: 0x%2, Bus: %3, Device: %4, Function: %5%7) %6
messages: An uncorrectable PCI express error detected on Port type: %1 (Segment: 0x%2, Bus: %3, Device: %4, Function: %5%7) %6
records.cause: An uncorrectable PCI express error detected.
records.recommended_action: Contact support if the issue persists.

event_names: The device in PCIe Slot %1 is SRIOV capable but is installed in a slot that does not support SRIOV
messages: The device in PCIe Slot %1 is single root input/output virtualization (SRIOV) capable but is installed in a slot that does not support SRIOV.
records.cause:
The PCIE slot or the installed CPU does not have ARI (Alternative Routing ID Interpretation) capability to
support SRIOV.
records.recommended_action:
Move this expansion card to an available slot that supports SRIOV, if SRIOV functionality is desired.
1.  Remove all power.
a.  Disconnect each power cord from the power source.
b.  Disconnect each power cord from the server
2.  Remove the expansion card.
3.  Install the expansion card in an available slot.
4.  Reconnect power and restart server.
For more information, see the troubleshooting guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website:
•  HPE ProLiant Gen10 (http://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-troubleshooting)
•  HPE Synergy (http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)

event_names: Data failed to load from the NVDIMM to volatile memory
messages: The persistent data restore failed and data is not available. Data is not lost unless the issue persists.
records.cause:
The data failed to load from the back-up non-volatile storage on the device to the regular, volatile memory
storage.
records.recommended_action:
Perform the following procedure for each affected DIMM.
1.  At the next available maintenance window power down your server.
2.  Remove all power.
a.  Disconnect each power cord from the power source.
b.  Disconnect each power cord from the server
3.  Remove the DIMM.
CAUTION: Failure to properly handle DIMMs can cause damage to DIMM components and the system
board connector.
See the DIMM handling guidelines on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise Library at: http://www.hpe.com/
info/enterprise/docs
4.  Clean the DIMM and the DIMM slot with anti-static compressed air.
5.  Reinstall the DIMM.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: NVDIMM backup power has been lost and a future backup is not possible
messages: NVDIMM backup power has been lost and a future backup is not possible. Data from the last successful backup is intact, but data modified after the last successful backup will be lost if power cannot be restored.
records.cause:
The backup battery is used to provide power to the NVDIMM-N modules in case of system power loss. Data
in the NVDIMM-N volatile memory must be backed up to the non-volatile flash storage prior to removing
power to the NVDIMM-N. If the backup battery goes bad or becomes disconnected, the backup is not
performed, and any modified data since the last backup is lost.
records.recommended_action:

messages: iLO requests the system to be powered on, but the Frame Link Module (FLM) or the Onboard Administrator (OA) are denying the request.
records.cause:
There are multiple causes for this condition:
•  Busy
•  Power hold
•  Insufficient cooling
•  Ekeying error
•  Enclosure error
•  Insufficient power
records.recommended_action:
Busy denial
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Enclosure Busy (Enclosure
Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)”.
•  This is not considered an error. It is used in Synergy and c-Class.
•  The Onboard Administrator or frame link module (FLM) is busy and not allowing iLO to power on the
server at this time.
•  Consult Onboard Administrator (c-Class) or OneView (Synergy).
Power hold
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Power Hold by Manager
Profile (Enclosure Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)”.
•  This is not considered an error (Synergy only).
•  OneView has applied a power hold to the bay the server is in and is currently in the process of
configuring the server's profile.
•  Consult OneView.
Insufficient Cooling Error
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Not Enough Cooling
(Enclosure Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)”.
•  There is not enough cooling in the frame (Synergy) or enclosure (c-Class).
•  There may be an issue with the fans in the frame.
•  Consult OneView (Synergy) or the Onboard Administrator (c-Class).
•  iLO will log an warning IML in this case when the denial reason occurs and set the health LED to
warning.
Ekeying Error
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Electronic Keying or I/O
Configuration Error (Enclosure Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)”.
•  There is a mismatch between the mezzanine cards and the interconnects in the frame or
enclosure. Applies to c-Class and Synergy.
•  This is due to a hardware configuration error.
•  Consult OneView (Synergy) or Onboard Administrator (c-Class).
•  This can be resolved by moving the server, the mezzanine cards, or the interconnects in the frame or
enclosure.
•  iLO will log a critical IML in this case when the denial reason occurs and set the health LED to critical.
Enclosure Error
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Enclosure Error <additional
information> (Enclosure Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)”.
•  There is an error in the frame (Synergy only).
•  Consult OneView for more information.
•  iLO will log an informational IML in this case when the denial reason occurs.
Insufficient Power
•  The message will read “Server Blade Enclosure Power Requested Denied: Not Enough Power
(Enclosure Serial Number <serial number>, Slot <blade slot location>)".
•  There is insufficient power in the frame or enclosure to allow the server to power on at this time.
•  This could be the result of the power supply configuration in the frame or enclosure.
•  Consult OneView (Synergy) or Onboard Administrator (c-Class).
•  This could resolve itself when the other servers run through POST.
•  iLO will log a critical IML in this case when the denial reason occurs and set the health LED to warning.
